acceptance_criteria: AC-1 THE DECISIVE TEST: a distinctive fixture secret written through create and replace-secret appears in no API response, CLI output, log line, audit row or exception over the whole cycle -- observed failing before the redaction/exclusion exists.
AC-2 A credential referenced by a credential_references row that a device uses cannot be deleted; an unreferenced one can.
AC-3 Secrets are AES-256-GCM encrypted under the store key from UI2_CREDENTIAL_STORE_KEY_FILE; a missing or empty key file stops start-up; decryption with a different key fails closed.

AC-4 Both discovery runners obtain their credential from the store through a credential_references id and refuse before any connect/keygen when it cannot be resolved; the environment-variable stand-ins are gone.
AC-5 HTTP and CLI cover create / list / replace-secret / delete with identical results, role:security_admin only, every mutation audited without the encrypted columns.
AC-6 The Administration screen's Credentials section lists and creates credentials with a write-only secret field; NoRoleConditionalRenderingInFrontendTest passes.
AC-7 The eleven-module build, :service:test, :cli:test, :worker:test, :architecture-tests:test and the frontend checks are green; privacy gate PASS.

report.objective: Build the product's credential store exactly as PO_DECISION_RECORD_2026_09_14 section 3 directs (CS-1 to CS-5): device and management-plane credentials created in the product's own interface (and CLI), encrypted at rest under an envelope key file with the same mechanism role bindings already use, never returned by anything, resolved only in the worker at execution time -- and replace the two discovery runners' environment-variable credential stand-ins with store-backed resolvers so a credential chosen in the product is the credential a run uses. This is the prerequisite of every device-add path (section 4).
output_contract: A credential store the operator fills from the product's own screen or CLI, encrypted at rest, never read back, that the discovery runners already consume.
One additive migration (V11), one resource on the existing service, CLI subcommands, two store-backed worker resolvers, one Administration screen section.
SESSION_CLOSE naming the migration columns, the key-file variable, the endpoints and subcommands, the audit exclusion mechanism, and the test counts before and after.

recommended_reasoning.reason: Four layers (migration, service, CLI, worker, frontend) around a secret-bearing boundary whose failures are silent -- a leaked field in one response, ciphertext in an audit row, a fallback left in place. Same class as the local identity administration movement; commit early so a budget stop is recoverable.

Every public type and method names the clause it implements (2026-09-14 record CS-n, 13C SB-n, 13G LIA-n, C1 section n).

No secret, passphrase or private key reaches a log line, an exception message, an audit row, an HTTP response, CLI output or a test assertion message.

The SESSION_CLOSE names the migration and its columns, the key-file variable, every endpoint and CLI subcommand, how the audit trigger excludes the encrypted columns, and the test counts before and after.
risks: Reusing the role-binding key for the store -- C1 section 6.1 scopes secrets per purpose; use a second key file.
Letting the audit trigger capture the encrypted columns, which puts ciphertext (and rotation history) into the audit table forever.
Returning the credential on create 'so the screen can show what was saved' -- the screen shows the row, never the secret.
Taking the secret from a CLI argument, which lands in shell history and process listings.
Leaving an environment-variable fallback in the runners 'for convenience' -- the runner must refuse before contact when the reference cannot be resolved.
Building a test-connection button here; it is a device contact and belongs to the device-add movement.

in: Migration V11 (additive only): a credentials table -- opaque id, display name, kind (closed set: ssh_password, ssh_private_key, api_password), username, encrypted secret (BYTEA), encrypted passphrase (BYTEA, nullable, ssh_private_key only), key id of the envelope key used, allowed vendors (closed vocabulary check_point | palo_alto, one or both), created_by actor, created_at, secret_set_at; the C1 section 3.5 audit trigger attached with the two encrypted columns EXCLUDED from what the trigger captures (say how in the SESSION_CLOSE). Extend secrets_metadata.backend_kind's CHECK with one new value for this store (CS-1's C1 successor) -- by dropping and re-adding the constraint in V11, never by editing V1.

Envelope: a CredentialStoreCipher (or GroupReferenceCipher reused with a distinct key) fed from ui2.credential-store.key-file (env UI2_CREDENTIAL_STORE_KEY_FILE, C1 section 6.2 _FILE convention, base64 256-bit, no default, start-up fails closed if the file is missing/empty). AES-256-GCM, fresh nonce per write, key id stored on the row so rotation is possible later.

Domain port in the module the local-identity administration lives in: create / list (names, kinds, vendors, username, timestamps -- NEVER the secret) / replace secret / delete; the create and replace operations take the secret as char[] or byte[] and zero it after encryption. CS-4: delete refuses with a distinct, non-identity-bearing status while any credential_references row points at the credential. A credential_references row is created for every stored credential (purpose = the kind, backend_pointer = the store row id) so B1_04B section 6 and every existing consumer of the reference model keep working.

HTTP API on the existing service, role:security_admin via the existing gate chain: POST /credentials, GET /credentials, POST /credentials/replace-secret, POST /credentials/delete. Every response body is scanned by a test for the absence of secret material. CLI parity on the existing CliEntryPoint: credential-create (secret from a prompt or a file argument, never a command-line argument), credential-list, credential-replace-secret, credential-delete -- sharing the domain port with the HTTP path.

Worker resolvers: a StoreBackedSshCredentialResolver and a StoreBackedPanCredentialResolver in worker that resolve a credentialRef (the credential_references id) by reading the store row and decrypting with the same envelope key file, returning the existing material records; the decrypted secret lives only as long as the connect/keygen call and is zeroed after. The two discovery runners (DiscoveryRunnerMain, PanDiscoveryRunnerMain) use the store-backed resolvers when UI2_CREDENTIAL_STORE_KEY_FILE and the database connection are available and refuse before contact when the reference cannot be resolved (SB-16); the environment-variable stand-ins are removed. The worker never logs a username or a secret.

Frontend: an Administration screen section 'Credentials' in the existing Material 3 vocabulary -- list (name, kind, vendors, username, when the secret was last set), create dialog (name, kind, vendors, username, secret; private key pasted or uploaded as text plus optional passphrase), replace-secret dialog, delete with the CS-4 refusal shown plainly. The secret field is write-only; nothing ever displays it back. NoRoleConditionalRenderingInFrontendTest must keep passing.

Tests, first two written FIRST and observed failing: (1) no API response, CLI output, log line, audit row or exception contains a stored secret or passphrase, proven over a full create-list-replace-resolve cycle with a distinctive fixture secret; (2) a credential referenced by a device cannot be deleted. Then: encrypt/decrypt round trip with the store key and refusal with the wrong key; a missing key file fails start-up closed; the store-backed SSH and PAN resolvers return the material the runners expect; CLI and HTTP produce the same rows; existing local-identity, role-binding, login and discovery tests stay green.
Commit early and often by layer (migration + cipher; domain + persistence; API; CLI; worker resolvers; frontend; tests). Open the PR at the end; do not merge.
out: Using the credential anywhere new: no device add flow, no enrollment confirm, no collection, no change to what the discovery runners DO once connected. Only how they obtain the credential changes.
Trust rules (SSH host-key fingerprints, TLS CA bundles/pins) -- keep the existing resolvers working; a trust store is a later movement.
Rotation policy, expiry, approval workflow, complexity rules, import from an external vault, or the 'vault_reference' backend (13G LIA-4 spirit; CS-5).
Editing any FROZEN document or any existing migration; a new Gradle subproject; a new external dependency (the JDK's javax.crypto and the existing bouncycastle suffice).
Returning, previewing, exporting or 'testing' a credential in a way that reveals it. A 'test connection' button is a device contact and belongs to the device-add movement.
